ap_statistics-f01.title: A placebo-controlled experiment on a new pain medicine

stimulus.description: Histogram of the number of minutes that patients reported pain relief for the patients that received the treatment.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: A researcher plans a new study of a new pain medicine in which each of $130$ patients will be given either a new pain medicine or a placebo, and the minutes of pain relief will be recorded for each. Identify the explanatory variable and the response variable, and say whether each is categorical or quantitative.
parts.model_answer: The explanatory variable is the type of pill (medicine or placebo), which is categorical. The response variable is the minutes of pain relief, which is quantitative.

common_errors: names the response as explanatory
classifies the type of pill as quantitative

parts.label: B

ap_statistics-f02.title: Voters who support a library bond: a binomial probability, the distribution of a sample proportion and an interval

stimulus.description: A polling organization knows from past surveys that about $35\%$ of the voters in a large county support a library bond.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Suppose that $10$ voters are selected at random from a very large population in which $35\%$ support a library bond. Let $X$ be the number of the voters who support a library bond. Identify the distribution of $X$ and calculate the probability that at least $3$ of the $10$ voters support a library bond. Round to three decimal places.
parts.model_answer: $X$ is binomial with $n = 10$ and $p = 0.35$. $P(X \ge 3) = 1 - P(X \le 2) \approx 0.738$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies a binomial distribution with n = 10 and p = 0.35
common_errors: gives p as a percent without converting
names a normal distribution

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates the probability of at least 3 (answer 0.738)
common_errors: computes P(X > 3)
computes P(X = 3)

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: A random sample of $200$ voters is selected from the population. State the mean and the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample proportion $\hat p$, and verify that the sampling distribution is approximately normal.
parts.model_answer: The mean is $0.35$ and the standard deviation is $\sqrt{0.35(1-0.35)/200} \approx 0.0337$. Both $np = 70.0$ and $n(1-p) = 130.0$ are at least $10$, so the sampling distribution is approximately normal.

rubric_rows.criterion: States the mean (answer 0.35) and calculates the standard deviation (answer 0.0337)

uses the sample proportion in place of p

rubric_rows.criterion: Verifies the large counts condition with np = 70.0 and n(1 - p) = 130.0, both at least 10

uses p-hat
